notes: The set coheres as one study, not a slideshow. The thread (healing through another's wounds, Isaiah 53:5 landed on Christ by 1 Peter 2:24) is carried unbroken: the felt ache opens (#1) and closes as healed (#14); the prophet sees it early (#2); the proof descends through the wounded/scourged Christ and the cross (#3,#5,#6); the apostle applies it (#7) without any invented eyewitness claim; the OT echoes are the passage's own (Isa 53:6 sheep #8, Isa 53:7 lamb #4, Acts 8:32). The 'we->ye' turn becomes a gaze (#11), and the landing lands on the cross/finished work and an open-handed invitation (#12,#13). The hero is the gospel-pivot cross (#6), bookending open and close so the Short lands on Christ. The only soft spot is a crucified-Christ cluster in the back half, which is intrinsic to Isaiah 53 and offset by framing variety and the non-Christ bookend — not a structural failure.
